mechanism: Both drugs are metabolized by CYP3A4; itraconazole inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase disulfiram levels, while disulfiram inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase itraconazole levels, leading to potential accumulation of both agents.
action: Monitor for increased disulfiram toxicity (peripheral neuropathy, hepatotoxicity) and itraconazole adverse effects; consider dose adjustment or therapeutic drug monitoring if co-administration is necessary.
